purpose: Corrects both the CRITICAL train/test overlap (heavy_r1) and the temporal-ordering blocker (fair_v1, REJECTED_TEMPORALLY_INELIGIBLE) findings with a leave-one-family-out cross-family protocol: zero request-level, event-level, AND temporal-direction risk, because held-out families never contribute any row at any stage.
central_rule: No request from the held-out test family F may contribute to model training, validation, hyperparameter selection, feature selection, horizon selection, seed selection, or early stopping.
Training and validation use only the other six families.
The trained model is frozen before any request from F is processed.
F is evaluated with history [0,10000) and score [10000,50000).
Exactly 40,000 requests contribute to the reported metric.
Cache and policy state survive the history/score boundary.
Metric counters reset at index 10000 without resetting cache/model state.
validation_rotation_rule: Sort all 7 family identifiers lexicographically. For the held-out test family at sorted index i, the validation family is the next family in cyclic order (index i+1 mod 7, excluding the test family itself, which cyclic-next never equals). The remaining 5 families are training. Deterministic, performance-independent, frozen before any training.
fold_isolation_invariants: held_out_test_family_rows == 0 in both training and validation datasets
test_family not in train_families and not in validation_family
global_statistic_rule: No preprocessing statistic (feature normalization, scaling, imputation constants) may be fit using all 7 families jointly. Any such statistic must be fit on the 5 training families of a given fold only. See docs/reviewer_fairness_cross_family_v1.md section 5 for the code audit confirming the reused feature-construction code has no such global-fit step to begin with.

training_family_weighting.rationale: The existing, reused build_evict_value_dataset_wulver_v1.py / assign_split pipeline does not implement per-family row-count equalization; it emits one row per (candidate, decision) naturally proportional to each family's request volume and unique-object count. Re-engineering equal-family-weighting (e.g. per-family subsampling to a common row budget) was considered but not implemented this session -- flagged as a documented, predeclared-before-training scope limitation, not a silent choice made after seeing results. This decision was frozen BEFORE any fold's dataset was built.
training_family_weighting.alternative_considered: A (equal rows per training family) was the task's stated preference; not implemented due to session time budget. If revisited, subsampling must be applied identically across all 7 folds' training splits, predeclared, and re-frozen as protocol version cross_family_v2.

hyperparameter_grid.source: reused unchanged from the canonical heavy_r1 search space (scripts/train_evict_value_wulver_v1.py: ridge, random_forest, hist_gb; scripts/build_evict_value_dataset_wulver_v1.py horizon default) -- not re-chosen after seeing any fold's held-out result, and not narrowed for this session's time budget the way fair_v1's scope was (this protocol keeps the full model-family set to preserve comparability with the original selection methodology).
hyperparameter_grid.horizon_note: Same scope-reduction rationale as fair_v1 (see docs/evict_value_v1_fair_training_protocol.md) -- a modeling prior, not leaked test information; applies identically to every fold.

amendment_policy: Any change to this protocol after viewing a held-out result requires a new protocol_id and a documented reason, mirroring the amendment policy already established for evict_value_v1_fair_v1.
